root_cause: The nightly batch workload consumed the available pgbouncer pool, leaving insufficient connections for interactive services.

actions.step: Scale payments-api and checkout-service to additional replicas.
Increase PostgreSQL max_connections to create more room for application traffic.
Restart pgbouncer and pause the overnight batch workload.

postmortem: The overnight batch consumed most pooled connections and caused interactive requests to wait until their deadlines expired. Scaling application pods did not help because it increased connection demand; pausing the batch and restarting pgbouncer restored capacity.

root_cause: An abandoned inactive replication slot prevented WAL recycling and filled the PostgreSQL data volume.

actions.step: Delete historical database and application logs from the volume.
Remove the confirmed abandoned replication slot that was retaining the WAL.
Expand the PostgreSQL PVC to provide additional emergency headroom.

postmortem: An abandoned replication slot held hundreds of gigabytes of WAL and pushed the database volume into critical disk pressure. Removing the slot stopped the retention, and expanding the PVC provided additional recovery headroom.
